newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil up on futures, Asia still draws producT.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil up on futures, Asia still draws producT.

text.p: NWE gas oil was pulled up on Friday by firmer futures and broadly steady premiums in a fairly quiet market.
May IPE gas oil last traded at $163.25 a tonne, $1 higher, supported from weather-related U.S heating oil gains.

Although business was slower compared with earlier in the week, diesel was reluctant to step out of the limelight. A cargo was sold at May IPE +$11 cif NWE with the market ranged between May IPE +$10-12 cif.
Russian premiums were pegged lower, although the market was not seen to have signficantly weakend.
"It has been a hard one to gauge because not much is going on but a cargo was done around May IPE +$2 cif NWE," said one dealer.
FOD and DIN were not attracting much interest at May IPE +$5 and +$4 respectively.
Concern over high freight rates and the tightening availability of tonnage.
Heating oil barges were slow with trades concluded at May IPE +25 and 50 cents for second half. First half May was still not widely talked, traders said.
